content.title: About
content.content: Beef and rice with gravy is a classic dish that combines tender pieces of beef, fluffy rice, and a savory gravy. The meal is rich in protein, carbohydrates, and B‑vitamins, making it a nourishing and satisfying option for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the most popular dietary sources of iron.
Rice, as a staple carbohydrate, provides a quick source of energy.
Traditional gravy is made from beef broth, onion, carrot, and spices.
The dish is commonly served in school cafeterias and family meals across Eastern Europe.
Combining beef and rice appears in many cuisines, from Russian to Japanese.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is highly bioavailable, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbohydrates
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbs that release energy slowly, helping maintain satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Zinc present in beef contributes to normal immune function.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Large portions of beef can raise cholesterol levels; choose lean cuts when possible.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt; monitor added sodium.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: A rare allergy to beef can cause reactions in some individuals.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure it is cooked thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often accompanied by a vegetable side. Fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon can brighten the flavor. Leftovers store well in the fridge and can be reheated in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
